inspection_summary: Inspected all 1060 normalized lines. The source develops four linked layers: a phase-space reconciliation of absorption and emission readings of the scaling Hamiltonian; quantized-calculus machinery yielding a semi-local trace formula; a diagnosis of why Li's positive-operator cutoff fails; and an operator-theoretic conjecture in which Poisson normalization, support conditions, and Sonine constructions may recover Weil positivity. Formula extraction is imperfect but the selected mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose, with figure or formula dependence recorded per unit.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the absorption/emission comparison, Li-attempt audit, and proposed semi-local operator-theoretic RH program.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates a return from global geometric methods to canonical semi-local Hilbert-space operators and previews the normalization obstruction.

sections_inspected.label: 1. The Scaling Hamiltonian
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates the PQ scaling generator and its cutoffs to white-light subtraction and the Berry-Keating phase-space count, while locating the residual sign in quantum phases.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Semi-local Trace Formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds quantized differentials, the semi-local quotient Hilbert space, Fourier factorization by local factors, dual cutoffs, and the resulting local trace decomposition.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Sonine Spaces and the Attempt of X.-J. Li
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns the proposed positive cutoff into an operator-sign and inner-function criterion, then proves the local factors fail that criterion and the desired inequality fails generally.

sections_inspected.label: 4. An Operator Theoretic Problem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Translates Weil positivity into constrained convolution form, states the semi-local conjecture, explains Poisson normalization and Sonine witnesses, and compares time/energy and analytic/geometric viewpoints.

sections_inspected.label: References and author metadata
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic provenance only; no additional semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Canonical semi-local operators and the normalization obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction distinguishes the artificial global Sobolev realization from canonical semi-local Hilbert-space operators, then identifies local principal-value normalization and the global Poisson formula as the likely missing ingredient in a positivity proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the full roadmap because the later technical sections separately realize each promised comparison, trace formula, failure diagnosis, and conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is self-contained; equation (0.1) only illustrates the semi-local unit group.

accepted_units.title: Quantization of PQ as the scaling generator and the need for two cutoffs
accepted_units.why_material: It identifies the symmetric quantization of PQ with the unitary scaling generator and explains why unboundedness prevents a discrete spectrum until matched position and momentum cutoffs are imposed.
accepted_units.context_note: Starts where the single-place semi-local model is introduced and ends after the cutoff phase-space region is specified.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The operator identification is clear in prose; precise Fourier normalization and phase-space boundary use displayed formulas.

accepted_units.title: Symplectic conversion of white light to scaling phase space
accepted_units.why_material: The exponential-coordinate symplectomorphism turns a cutoff regular representation into a hyperbolic PQ region, providing the representation bridge needed to compare background white light with the spectral model.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the setup, explicit map, Jacobian check, and interpretation of the transformed region.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends partly on Figures 3-4 for the region shape, but the map and symplectic calculation are textually recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Two finite phase-space discrepancies and the one-state rectangle
accepted_units.why_material: The comparison isolates a high-momentum excess and a unit-area rectangle, clarifying exactly what differs between the cutoff absorption region and cutoff white light before rescaling.
accepted_units.context_note: The footnote immediately after the span gives a suggestive pole/boundary-condition analogy but is supporting context rather than part of the geometric comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly figure-dependent; prose gives the bounds and unit area, but scan verification would help confirm the shaded regions.

accepted_units.title: Area-preserving rescaling recovers the Berry-Keating missing region
accepted_units.why_material: A symplectic rescaling preserving PQ and area converts the excess white-light region into the Berry-Keating semiclassical picture, showing equality of the zero-count asymptotics without asserting model equivalence.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends at the authors' explicit warning that semiclassical agreement does not make the quantum models equivalent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The rescaling formula and conclusion are readable; Figure 6 and the imported Figure 7 carry the detailed geometry.

accepted_units.title: The absorption sign survives in Maslov phases
accepted_units.why_material: The text separates semiclassical count agreement from quantum fluctuations: the emission description must encode the absorption minus sign through a uniform Maslov-phase choice.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the end of the phase-space comparison to preserve the contrast between agreement and nonequivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dependent; the quoted external discussion is omitted after the colon by the extraction, so the selected claim is limited to the authors' stated conclusion.

accepted_units.title: Quantized differential as a graded commutator calculus
accepted_units.why_material: It replaces ordinary differentiation by commutation with a self-adjoint involution and shows how graded forms retain nilpotence, furnishing the reusable operator-calculus abstraction used later.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the general algebraic definition before specialization to one variable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed products are mildly degraded but their algebraic content is recoverable from surrounding prose.

accepted_units.title: One-variable Hilbert-transform commutator kernel
accepted_units.why_material: The abstract differential is realized by the Hilbert transform, with a difference-quotient kernel that converts regularity of functions into operator properties.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Fourier projection setup, principal-value Hilbert transform, definition, and kernel.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula typography is imperfect, especially the integral, but the commutator and kernel are legible.

accepted_units.title: Quantized calculus on modulated groups
accepted_units.why_material: The one-variable construction is generalized to any locally compact abelian group with a proper modulus, replacing the Hilbert transform by a Fourier-conjugated modulus projection.
accepted_units.context_note: Line 434 is shared with the preceding specialization because it is the transition sentence defining the scope of the generalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the displayed Fourier-conjugation formulas; their operator order remains recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Semi-local adèle-class quotient and scaling action
accepted_units.why_material: It removes the additive/multiplicative Haar singularity by restricting to finitely many places, forms the quotient XS by S-units, and equips it with the natural multiplicative action and self-dual additive pairing.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the full geometric setup needed for the later Hilbert space and Fourier operator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Some product and exponent placement is typographically degraded, but all objects and quotient relations are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Unitary Fourier and regular-representation models of L2(XS)
accepted_units.why_material: The additive Fourier transform descends unitarily to L2(XS), while a second unitary identification converts the nonunitary scaling action into the regular representation with an explicit modulus factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 2.2 and the intertwining identity that later permits trace computation on the modulated group.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Operator equations are readable; the prose fixes the direction of the intertwiner.

accepted_units.title: Fourier transform factors through inversion and local L-factor ratios
accepted_units.why_material: It packages each local additive Fourier transform as inversion plus multiplicative convolution by a unitary local-factor ratio, then tensors these into the semi-local operator factorization of Lemma 2.3.
accepted_units.context_note: The product function and projection maps are included so the factorization does not rely on unstated local data.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several dual-group decorations are degraded; the factorization order and local-factor interpretation are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Dual infrared and ultraviolet cutoffs become a truncated quantized differential
accepted_units.why_material: The physical-space cutoff and its Fourier conjugate are combined, and Lemma 2.4 converts their sandwiched scaling action into truncated projections around the quantized logarithmic derivative of the local-factor product.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definitions of both cutoffs and all notation needed to interpret the operator identity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (2.27) has line-break and symbol loss; later prose reliably identifies the central operator, but exact constants should be checked against the scan before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Product-rule decomposition yields a sum of local trace terms
accepted_units.why_material: The quantized logarithmic derivative obeys a product decomposition, turning a single operator trace into the sum of placewise principal-value contributions used in the explicit formula.
accepted_units.context_note: Kept separate from the theorem to expose the local-to-semi-local mechanism rather than only its endpoint.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed product rule and trace integral are OCR-fragile; the sum-over-places mechanism is clear from checked prose.

accepted_units.title: Semi-local trace formula with logarithmic main term
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2.5 identifies the asymptotic trace of the cutoff scaling action with a universal logarithmic term plus normalized local explicit-formula distributions, and then rewrites them symmetrically in the test function h.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theorem and the immediate change of test-function normalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula extraction loses some integral formatting, but variables, local sum, main term, and symmetric rewrite are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Li's positive-operator strategy from finite-place localization
accepted_units.why_material: Compact support reduces the explicit formula to finitely many places, while positivity of trace-class products suggests proving Weil's inequality through a balanced near-zero cutoff in the semi-local model.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the two foundational facts and the target inequality, stopping before its operator realization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The target integral is formula-dependent and typographically degraded; its intended sign and convolution form are explicit.

accepted_units.title: The cutoff proposal reduces positivity to the sign of a logarithmic derivative
accepted_units.why_material: The convolution test function gives a positive multiplication operator, and Li's replacement cutoff would prove the desired inequality precisely if its positive compression equaled minus one half of the quantized logarithmic derivative.
accepted_units.context_note: Supplies the bridge between the general positive-product fact and the exact operator-sign criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Operator notation is readable despite broken display alignment.

accepted_units.title: Negative quantized logarithmic derivative iff Hardy-subspace invariance
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 3.4 proves equivalence among the cutoff identity, negativity of the logarithmic derivative, and invariance of the projected subspace; Corollary 3.5 identifies the one-variable condition with innerness.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the complete equivalence proof and its Beurling-space specialization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof is recoverable from operator prose; a few fractions and commutator marks are visually degraded.

accepted_units.title: Local-factor ratios have boundary modulus one but are not inner
accepted_units.why_material: Both finite-prime and archimedean local-factor ratios are unimodular on the critical line yet fail Hardy innerness through poles or unbounded growth, directly invalidating the criterion needed by the cutoff proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes distinct finite and infinite-place diagnoses because together they rule out every local factor used by the proposed method.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gamma-factor displays and the numerical example are formula-sensitive; holomorphy and unboundedness conclusions are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: The desired inequality would force false monotonicity of the Riemann-Siegel phase
accepted_units.why_material: Beyond failure of the proof mechanism, Fact 3.6 shows the inequality itself fails generally: in the archimedean case it would force a constant-sign logarithmic derivative and hence monotonicity of the Riemann-Siegel angle.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with the conclusion about failed innerness to preserve the distinction between criterion failure and falsity of the unrestricted inequality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The final nonmonotonicity evidence invokes Figure 8; the logical reduction to monotonicity is textually clear, while the graph should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Support-restricted Weil positivity as a finite semi-local problem
accepted_units.why_material: Weil's criterion is rewritten as a convolution square with two moment constraints, motivating the conjecture that places below a support-determined threshold suffice for the corresponding test functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the equivalence, change to the symmetric h-normalization, constraints, and Conjecture 4.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several integrals are line-broken but the convolution form, vanishing moments, support interval, and finite set of places remain recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Poisson summation produces the archimedean local-factor ratio
accepted_units.why_material: The scaling-equivariant theta-like map E becomes multiplication by zeta in multiplicative Fourier variables, while Poisson conjugacy of additive Fourier transform with inversion forces their quotient, explaining the local-factor ratio conceptually.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the self-dual character normalization, Fourier representation of E, and functional-equation identification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact Mellin/Fourier exponents are formula-dependent but sufficiently legible; the derivation is explicitly labeled formal by the authors.

accepted_units.title: Semi-local Poisson summation fixes character normalization on the quotient
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing integers by QS decomposes the sum into S-units and a complementary monoid, removes selected Euler factors, and shows why different self-dual character choices become equivalent after quotienting by S-units.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends with the explicit inference that Poisson normalization should be central to Conjecture 4.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The partial Euler product is formula-sensitive; the unit decomposition and character-independence argument are prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Poisson distributions and the scaling Hamiltonian generate Sonine elements
accepted_units.why_material: A differential operator enforcing simultaneous value and Fourier-value constraints transforms the Poisson comb into distributions supported away from zero; smoothing gives Schwartz Sonine functions, and a Fourier-symmetric polynomial in the scaling generator supplies a canonical choice.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the construction, why the simpler derivative is asymmetric, the corrected scaling-Hamiltonian operator, and its geometric-side remark.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted definition near line 948 has a parenthesis defect, but equation (4.8) and the surrounding prose recover the operator; formula-level use should verify the scan.

accepted_units.title: Zeta zeros are naturally times in the function-field analogue
accepted_units.why_material: The function-field model turns zeros into periodic arithmetic progressions in the imaginary coordinate, supporting the scaling approach's dual interpretation of zeros as times rather than energy levels.
accepted_units.context_note: The example is used only for the time-versus-energy conceptual comparison, not as evidence for the number-field RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layout is degraded but periodicity and dependence on arguments modulo 2π are clear.

accepted_units.title: Analytic support exploitation versus global geometric structure
accepted_units.why_material: The closing comparison identifies a plausible analytic next step and its vulnerability to principal-value normalization errors, while explaining what the global geometric model adds: an interpretation of scaling as Frobenius on the Scaling Site.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the authors' uncertainty; it is a comparison of research routes, not a claimed proof strategy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is self-contained.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Semiclassical equivalence with a quantum sign remainder
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Quantizing PQ and subtracting cutoff white light reproduce the Berry-Keating semiclassical region after symplectic changes of representation, but the absorption sign remains detectable in quantum phases.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This establishes agreement of semiclassical counting pictures, not spectral equivalence or RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local-factor quantized differentials generate the semi-local explicit formula
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After the semi-local quotient turns scaling into a modulated regular representation, additive Fourier transform factors through local L-ratios, and the product rule for their quantized logarithmic derivative decomposes the cutoff trace into explicit-formula terms place by place.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several displayed constants and principal-value normalizations require scan verification before formal reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Why positive compression cannot directly prove Weil positivity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Li's cutoff strategy would need negativity of a quantized logarithmic derivative, equivalently innerness of the local-factor ratios, but those ratios are unbounded or have poles; moreover the unrestricted target inequality itself would falsely force monotonicity of the Riemann-Siegel phase.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The failure is of this unrestricted semi-local positivity route and does not imply failure of support-restricted variants.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Poisson normalization as the missing constraint for a support-restricted route
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The support-restricted Weil problem is finite-place, while Poisson summation both produces the local-factor ratios and removes basic-character ambiguity on the semi-local quotient, suggesting a principled source for the principal-value normalization absent from the failed cutoff argument.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This motivates Conjecture 4.1 but supplies neither its operator inequality nor a proof.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Scaling dynamics links analytic Sonine constraints and geometric Frobenius
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A Fourier-symmetric polynomial in the scaling generator constructs Sonine-type constrained functions, while the same scaling viewpoint reads zeros as times and acquires a Frobenius interpretation globally.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The connections are conceptual bridges across analytic and geometric viewpoints, not an established transfer of positivity between them.

stop_reason: All usable mathematical prose from the introduction through Section 4.3 has been represented: further segmentation would split proofs into routine operator algebra, duplicate theorem setup already retained, isolate figure/page furniture, or select bibliography. Formula- and figure-dependent spans with recoverable semantics were retained with explicit scan-verification limits; no unreadable span contains a distinct unrepresented mechanism.
